name: Turkish
script: Latin with extra letters: ç, ğ, ı, İ, ö, ş, ü; left to right
basis: University beginner Turkish: Ohio State Turkish 1101 (Öztopçu, Elementary Turkish) and Hashemite University Turkish for Beginners 1 (Yedi İklim Türkçe A1)
src: Ohio State University, Turkish 1101 syllabus AU16 (PDF), textbook Öztopçu, Elementary Turkish: weekly order of alphabet, vowel harmony, 'to be', plurals, questions, locative, consonant alternation, genitive and possessives, present progressive, dative, var / yok, imperative, -mak istemek, ablative, accusative, past tense

Hashemite University (Jordan), Turkish for Beginners 1 course plan (PDF), textbook Yedi İklim Türkçe A1: greetings and alphabet, vowel harmony, mı / mi, bu / şu / o, plurals, numbers and days, present continuous, dative and nerede / nereden / nereye, nationalities, ablative
note: The order follows the OSU sequence, with greetings first and the demonstrative and numbers lessons placed as in the Hashemite plan. Giving -lı / -sız and the ordering-food lesson their own places, and the directions lesson, are common course practice and my own judgment, as are all titles.
hardest: Vowel harmony: every suffix changes its vowel (-lar / -ler, -da / -de, -ı / -i / -u / -ü)
Word order with the verb last, and long words built from many suffixes
Consonant changes at the end of words: kitap → kitabım, çocuk → çocuğum
Dotted i and dotless ı, and the silent ğ

items: Alphabet and sounds: ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü
Greetings: merhaba, günaydın, Nasılsınız?; sen and siz
The question particle mı / mi / mu / mü
bu, şu, o: Bu ne? Bu kim?
Plurals and question words: -lar / -ler; ne, kim, nerede, kaç
Numbers and prices: Kaç lira? Ne kadar?
var and yok: there is, there isn't
Consonant softening: kitap → kitabım, çocuk → çocuğum
Present continuous -iyor: geliyorum, gelmiyorum, geliyor musun?
Ordering food: … istiyorum, -mak istemek, Hesap lütfen
Time and days: Saat kaç? pazartesi
